assertion_analysis.failure_condition: Returning an always-empty excerpt from should_trigger_fanout makes the excerpt and prompt assertions red; logs/negative-control.log records this mutation failing test_prompt_names_the_checks_that_fired.
Inventing a reason when the trigger does not fire, or dropping the (none) fallback at dispatcher.py:92, reddens the check-free test.
Removing the check.retrieval filter at trigger.py:118 reddens the non-retrieval test, which asserts the identifier never reaches the prompt.

Dropping the veto filter at trigger.py:95 makes the passing check appear in the excerpt and fires on it; logs/negative-control-veto-filter.log records this exact mutation failing this test and test_a_lone_passing_check_cannot_fire_the_trigger.
Treating a non-vetoed entry as a failure at any threshold makes the lone-passing-check assertions red; the veto-filter control log shows it.

Removing the truncation or the check-count break in trigger.py:136-138 yields eight long lines and reddens the cap test, but the expected values are the module's own constants, so the budget itself is not pinned.

findings.text: non-blocking: the cap test compares the produced line count and line lengths against _EXCERPT_MAX_CHECKS and _EXCERPT_MAX_CHARS imported from the module under test (also used at line 227), so it proves a cap is applied but passes unchanged if the budget is raised; literal 6 and 240 on the expected side would make the budget the guarded value.
